content.title: Peer Group Mentoring
content.summary: Peer Group Mentoring pairs participants with experienced open‑source veterans in small pods to discuss technical, community, career, and certification topics, fostering inclusive skill development and networking across CNCF projects. This session matters because it builds a supportive ecosystem that helps Kubernetes users and operators grow their expertise and confidence.
content.description:
Peer Group Mentoring allows participants to meet with experienced open source veterans across many CNCF projects. Mentees are paired with 2 – 10 other people in a pod-like setting to explore technical, community, career, and certification questions together.

If you're interested in being a Mentor, please sign up. 
If you're interested in attending as a Mentee, seating is on a first come, first served basis.

content.title: Project Pavilion Tour
content.summary: The session provides a guided tour of the Project Pavilion, connecting attendees with project maintainers, showcasing community engagement practices, explaining how KCD events are organized, and highlighting certification paths for contributors. This matters to Kubernetes users and operators because it helps them discover new projects, build relationships, and find ways to deepen their involvement and credibility in the ecosystem.
content.description: Explore the Project Pavilion, a hub of innovation and discovery! Take part in daily tours, interact with project maintainers at their kiosks, gain insights on community engagement and KCD event organization, and learn more about certification opportunities to showcase your expertise.This tour will include an introduction to the Pavilion, making introductions, interacting with maintainers, and ensuring you end up talking to the right projects!

This matters to Kubernetes operators because it offers a Kubernetes‑native way to secure and govern AI workloads at scale while maintaining continuous compliance.

As AI agents evolve from experiments to autonomous actors in complex systems, they strain traditional authorization models. How can we empower them while enforcing least privilege and governance?

This session introduces agentgateway, a dataplane powered by kgateway that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and integrates with CNCF policy engines like Kyverno. content.author: Arun Gupta & Jan-Niklas Wortmann
content.summary: The session demonstrates how to containerize and operate multi‑agent AI workflows on Kubernetes, mapping architectures to Deployments, Services/Ingress, ConfigMaps and Secrets, and showcasing A/B testing, cost‑aware metrics, OpenTelemetry observability, HPA‑driven autoscaling, and secure agent‑to‑agent communication via a service mesh with traffic‑splitting and hot‑swappable model rollouts.

In enterprise environments, ambiguity creates a critical security vulnerability that makes fine-grained authorization and audit impossible. Traditional static API keys simply can’t capture the full context behind an action. content.title: Unifying Inner & Outer Loops To Bridge the Gaps Between Devs & Ops With Microcks + Score

content.summary: The session demonstrates how to unify the inner (local) and outer (cluster) development loops using Score to generate Docker‑Compose files and Kubernetes manifests, and Microcks to provide realistic contract‑driven mocks for missing or third‑party services. By keeping specifications in sync across environments, teams can catch integration issues early, reduce "works on my machine" problems, and accelerate cloud‑native application delivery, illustrated with a live Finos/TraderX use case.

content.author: John Clark
content.summary: This case‑study details how Skyscanner re‑architected its east‑west traffic at massive scale (over 60 M requests per minute) by replacing AWS NLBs with a pod‑to‑pod multicluster model, deploying Istio Ambient Mesh for sidecar‑less zero‑trust, and adding gateway‑API based ingress/egress, achieving major cost savings while maintaining resilience, compliance, and observability via OpenTelemetry.
content.description:
At Skyscanner scale, every architecture choice carries cost and ops impact. Running dozens of Kubernetes clusters and >60M req/min, we were stuck with costly, complex east-west NLBs. This talk shows how we rebuilt our network to save millions on AWS while preserving resilience and compliance, and how we balanced cost, performance, and auditability.

content.author: Giedrius Statkevičius
content.summary: The session explains how integrating Parquet as a columnar storage backend for Thanos can dramatically speed up large‑scale PromQL queries and reduce storage costs, covering architecture, migration steps, performance benchmarks, and the roadmap for future Parquet support.
content.description: Large PromQL queries over months of data can easily take tens of seconds in huge scale Thanos deployments. content.summary: The session reviews the new capabilities introduced in Helm 4, explains the strategic direction of the Helm project, and outlines how users and contributors can get involved in its future development, which is critical for anyone relying on Helm for Kubernetes application lifecycle management.

content.summary: The panel explores how SIG Contributor Experience (ContribEx) supports and retains Kubernetes contributors through sub‑projects focused on automation, mentoring, elections, governance, communications, and events, illustrating the journey from a first PR to a sense of belonging. content.description: Kubernetes is supported by a wide contributor community, and the structures that guide the community can be hard to understand at first. SIG Contributor Experience helps connect those pieces through sub-projects focused on communication, workflow, and governance. content.author: Yong Tang

It provides operators with practical guidance to keep DNS reliable and secure, a foundational service for Kubernetes workloads.
content.description: Recent DNS disruptions at major cloud providers highlight how sensitive DNS is as a foundational dependency for modern internet and Kubernetes platforms. Even brief degradation can cascade into widespread application failures, reinforcing the need to treat DNS itself as a critical infrastructure. In this session, we’ll examine how CoreDNS is evolving to meet these demands in large-scale, critical cloud environments. content.author: Kateryna Hrytsaienko

content.author: LeRenzo Malcom & Mario Flores
content.summary: This session presents a real‑world case study of how Enpal built a cloud‑native Virtual Power Plant platform that orchestrates hundreds of thousands of residential solar, battery, and EV‑charging IoT devices. content.description:
Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) are reshaping the energy grid by turning thousands of distributed IoT devices—solar systems, batteries, EV chargers—into one coordinated, cloud-native asset. At Enpal, we operate one of Europe’s largest residential solar fleets and are building a next-generation VPP platform to orchestrate it.

In software development, we often focus on functional requirements – what the application does. But let’s be real: it’s the non-functional requirements (NFRs) that make or break an application’s success in the long run. For cloud-native applications, things like scalability, resilience, observability, and security aren’t just “nice-to-haves” – they’re the foundation of performance, maintainability, and availability.

content.description: Industry analysis reveals that expensive GPU cards are often utilized for processing simple queries that could efficiently be handled by CPUs, such as batch processing, non-real-time requests, or small context queries. content.description: In this session we'll learn how Dapr enables agent frameworks like OpenAI agents, AWS Strands, CrewAI and LangGraph to run reliably in the face of network errors, full cluster shutdowns and even complete cloud outages. content.author: Amy Chen

It equips operators with a mental model and practical tools to diagnose connectivity, performance, and security issues in any cluster.

Using simple diagrams and live command-line demos, we’ll trace a packet’s journey across nodes and clusters to reveal how traffic actually flows in Kubernetes.

Telco hard standards often clash with Kubernetes best practices.
